stem.text: A file downloads at a rate of D(t) megabytes per second, where D is differentiable and t is measured in seconds. Measured values are D(0) = 12, D(5) = 16, D(10) = 10, D(15) = 8. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{15} D(t)\,dt \), the number of megabytes downloaded from t = 0 to t = 15, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 5 \cdot \frac{12 + 16}{2} = 70 \); \( 5 \cdot \frac{16 + 10}{2} = 65 \); \( 5 \cdot \frac{10 + 8}{2} = 45 \).

distractor_derivations.A: factor 1/2 applied to the first trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.C: left Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
distractor_derivations.D: trapezoid area taken as width times the sum of the two endpoint values, with no division by 2
